citations.title: Who is an 'employee' (includes managerial and supervisory staff)
citations.plain: Under the Code on Wages, 'employee' covers anyone an establishment employs on wages for skilled, unskilled, manual, clerical, technical, supervisory, managerial or administrative work. Managers and senior staff therefore count as employees. Apprentices and members of the Armed Forces do not.

citations.title: No salary ceiling for the timely-payment and deduction rules
citations.plain: The old Payment of Wages Act protected only employees earning up to Rs 24,000 a month. Under the Code on Wages, the rules on paying wages on time and on permitted deductions apply to all employees, whatever their salary. The labour ministry has confirmed that this includes white-collar staff.

citations.title: Deadline for paying wages, including after leaving the job
citations.plain: Wages are due by these deadlines: daily workers at the end of the shift; weekly workers on the last working day of the week; fortnightly workers before the end of the second day after the fortnight; monthly workers before the end of the 7th day of the next month. If you are removed, dismissed, retrenched or resign, or lose your job because the establishment closes, your wages must be paid within two working days.

citations.title: Filing a wage claim: who decides it and the 3-year limit
citations.plain: Wage claims under the Code are heard by an authority the Government appoints, who must be at least a Gazetted Officer. The claim can be filed by you, your registered trade union, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator. File within 3 years of the date the claim arises; a later claim may still be accepted if you show sufficient cause. Besides the amount due, the authority can award compensation of up to ten times the claim, and it tries to decide within three months.

draft.title: Legal Notice for Unpaid Salary
draft.body_markdown:
**LEGAL NOTICE** (By Registered Post A.D.)

Date: [[FILL: date]]

**From:**
[[FILL: Your Full Name]]
[[FILL: Your Complete Residential Address]]
Phone: [[FILL: Your Phone Number]]
Email: [[FILL: Your Email Address]]

**To:**
[[FILL: HR/Employer Name]]
Startup Company in Noida
[[FILL: Company Registered Address]]
Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India

**Subject:** Demand for payment of unpaid salary for August & September 2026 and full & final settlement.

1. I was employed by the above‑named startup as a **Software Developer** on the terms stated in the offer letter dated [[FILL: offer letter date]].
2. My agreed monthly salary was **₹70,000** per month, as reflected in the salary slips for the months prior to August 2026.
3. I submitted my resignation on **30 September 2026**, which was also my last working day, as per the resignation submission record.
4. The salary for the months of **August 2026** and **September 2026** (total **₹1,40,000**) has not been paid to date.
5. I have repeatedly requested payment from the HR department. The HR representative replied that the company is currently incurring losses and the dues will be cleared later, but no concrete date or payment has been provided.
6. I possess the following documentary evidence: the original offer letter, salary slips for the months prior to August 2026, and the email communication from HR indicating the delay.

**Legal Basis**
Under the **Code on Wages, 2019**, an *employee* includes any person engaged on wages for skilled or unskilled work (s.2(k)). The Code applies to all employees irrespective of salary level (Fact‑COW‑NO‑WAGE‑CEILING). Section 17 of the Code mandates that monthly wages must be paid **before the end of the 7th day of the next month**. My salary for August and September 2026 became due on **7 October 2026** and **7 November 2026** respectively, both of which have long passed (COW2019‑S17).

**Demand**
I hereby demand payment of the full unpaid salary amounting to **₹1,40,000** within **15 days** from the receipt of this notice. Payment should be made by direct bank transfer to the following account:

Account Holder: [[FILL: Your Name]]
Account Number: [[FILL: Your Bank Account Number]]
IFSC Code: [[FILL: Your Bank IFSC]]
Bank Name: [[FILL: Your Bank Name]]

**Consequences of Non‑Compliance**
If the amount is not received within the stipulated period, I will be compelled to pursue all lawful remedies available to me, including:
- Filing a wage claim before the appropriate labour authority under **Section 45** of the Code on Wages, 2019 (COW2019‑S45);
- Initiating a civil suit for recovery of wages within the three‑year limitation period (Limitation Act 1963, Article 7);
- Seeking recovery of costs and interest as permitted by law.

All expenses incurred in pursuing these remedies will be borne by the employer.

**Copy retained for record.**

______________________________
[[FILL: Your Full Name]]
Phone: [[FILL: Your Phone Number]]
Email: [[FILL: Your Email Address]]

citations.title: Filing a wage claim: who decides it and the 3-year limit

The claim can be filed by you, your registered trade union, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator. send_instructions: 1. इस नोटिस को रजिस्टर्ड पोस्ट (रिटर्न रिसीट के साथ) द्वारा कंपनी के पंजीकृत पते पर भेजें।
2. पोस्टिंग के बाद रिटर्न रिसीट की एक कॉपी सुरक्षित रखें; यह डिलीवरी प्रमाण के रूप में काम करेगी।
3. यदि 15 दिनों के भीतर कोई उत्तर नहीं मिलता, तो SAMADHAN पोर्टल (https://samadhan.labour.gov.in) पर wage claim दर्ज करें और रिटर्न रिसीट की स्कैन की हुई कॉपी अपलोड करें।
4. साथ ही, 3 साल की सीमित अवधि के भीतर सिविल suit दायर करने की तैयारी करें; आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ (ऑफ़र लेटर, सैलरी स्लिप, HR ई‑मेल) को क्रमबद्ध रखें।
5. यदि आर्थिक कठिनाई हो तो 15100 (NALSA) पर कॉल करके मुफ्त कानूनी सहायता या लोक अदालत (Lok Adalat) के माध्यम से निपटारा करने की जानकारी प्राप्त करें।
